key_insight: Input-convex neural surrogates make learned safety and comfort costs tractable within optimization-based lane-changing trajectory planning.
engineering_relevance: The framework supports efficient trajectory planning for connected and automated vehicles interacting with uncertain human-driven traffic.
method: Plan lane changes using Bézier curves and learned safety and lateral-comfort costs.
Combine input-convex recurrent, fully input-convex, and partially input-convex networks to model trajectory, duration, and traffic history.
Embed surrogates through linear-programming formulations without binary variables, with exactness at optimality established theoretically.
evidence_signal: Tests on combined real-world and simulated trajectories report competitive surrogate accuracy and faster optimization than conventional MIPs; closed-loop simulations report lower weighted planning costs than baselines.
watch_item: Exact surrogate embedding does not guarantee real-world safety; robustness to traffic behavior outside the training distribution requires validation.
paper_title: Optimization-based lane-changing trajectory planning in mixed traffic with embedded input convex neural networks
